report.math_notes: Checked the argument step by step. Lemma A (reduction to m_i' = lcm of the pairwise gcds): (1)-(4) are correctly proved; disjointness is preserved because g_ij | m_i', m_j' so a_i'-a_j' ≡ a_i-a_j (mod g_ij). Lemma B (density criterion): the M/d_i translates a_i+t m_i are pairwise incongruent mod M via gcd(M/d_i, m_i/d_i)=1; pigeonhole gives a_i-a_j = s m_j - t m_i + uM, divisible by g_ij since g_ij | m_i, m_j, M — correct, and it is correctly applied to sub-families (a sub-family of a disjoint family is disjoint, and M need only be a multiple of the gcds inside the sub-family). Lemma C trivial. Corollary D correctly reduces the existence of a size-k counterexample to a non-decreasing k-tuple of divisors of L_k satisfying (R1)-(R3),(R5). I read code_1: candidati = divisors ≥2 of lcm(1..k-1); prefix pruning uses exactly (R1) and Lemma B on the prefix with every divisor M of L_k that is a multiple of the lcm of the prefix gcds (valid); leaves apply (R3) and Lemma B on every sub-multiset; exact integer arithmetic; repeated moduli allowed (m ≥ last). The implementation matches the proved rules, and no unproved rule is used (M4/M5 off). Hence 'zero stage-A survivors for 3 ≤ k ≤ 12' ⇒ theorem for k ≤ 12 is a valid inference. The k=13 hand proof for the 7-class part (10,10,10,10,10,12,45) is correct: five disjoint classes mod 10 are distinct mod 10; either they cover Z/5 (then the mod-45 class, gcd 5, meets one) or two coincide mod 5 and differ by 5, hence have opposite parity, and the mod-12 class (gcd 2) meets one.
